title: Measure authorized burst-survival scenarios
description:
Reproduce selected microfrag.10 burst scenarios on a specifically authorized test setup using the approved profile and measured resource budgets. Compare baseline and experimental delivery under the same conditions, including header loss and shared-receiver contention. Produce evidence for a human prototype/revise/reject disposition.

HPC8 execution policy: Code, test, or schema changes require three independent correctness, security, and robustness reviews; file and fix all findings and re-review. Use independent oracles, never weakened legacy tests or self-generated expected results. Preserve upstream Yggdrasil addressing, radio-owned identity, best-effort custody, baseline SCHC, and the human-only OSCORE/EDHOC security edit bar. External actions, hardware/RF operations, and port access require scoped explicit permission and applicable bench safety checks. Research may conclude no-go; an authorization gate requires affirmative, recorded approval for its actual scope. Dependency closure and decomposition are not permission. No speculative activation, including deferred portability or experimental modes.
design: Require matching affirmative microfrag.06, authority.10 and rf.03 approvals for this session. Ports, interfering test signals and field RF each need explicit applicable permission; no such action is implicit. If clearance is denied, expired or mismatched, keep execution blocked or deferred.
acceptance_criteria: Known transmitted bytes and independent RF/loss observations establish actual recovered payloads and failed deliveries. Report latency, CPU/memory, complete airtime and per-frequency occupancy costs with uncertainty. A successful FEC case proves neither capacity scaling nor compliance or final equipment authorization.
